Documentation-only change to docs/architecture/inference.md (head lines 25-171 add Nemotron Super local-path prose; base lines 831-1204 and head lines 1-400 are mostly unchanged context). No code, config, or control changes are visible. The new text says the paths are unregistered, unwired and not installed by any production caller (head 34-35, 105), with the local image HTTP hook defaulting to absent (head 101).

Security-relevant claims that later passes should check against code:
1. Head 131-142: an optional resident recurrent checkpoint bank is gated by DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE_MEMORY=1. Text requests then use the 'local unscoped cache scope'. T-041 says production has no RAM prefix tier, and that scope is coordinator-authored from authenticated account. The new prose describes an unscoped resident cache, so cross-caller reuse and a TTFT oracle on the local authenticated HTTP hook (head 100-105) fall outside T-041's scope. This is not production-wired on the supplied evidence, so I record it as an unverified contract rather than a finding. If the hook or the memory flag ever reaches production, T-041 and SEC-035 need updating.
2. Head 100-112: local HTTP hook admission is bounded (429 queueFull) and relies on existing local authentication. Authentication code is not supplied.
3. Head 147-170: DARKBLOOM_NEMOTRON_SUPER_MTP is an opt-in that adds memory charges (a 256 MiB unmeasured scratch allowance); the claim is that charges are admitted before allocation.
4. Head 82-92: encoded image ingress is charged and bounded before decode, and accepts only PNG/JPEG data URIs. This is relevant to T-050 (the claim that no temporary files are written), but no decode or temp-file code is supplied.

The patch excerpt is truncated and the head excerpt ends at line 401, so I could not examine the rest of the head file. The only head change after line 171 is at 876-877, which is outside the supplied head text. Underlying source files were not supplied, so the doc claims are unverified.
